flags.reason: Same TV suggestion given a third time (lines 22, 52, 57) after participant showed little interest; pushes advice.
Sustain talk about not changing diet at his age went unexplored; coach moved straight on.
Guilt and wanting energy back is strong change talk; coach responded only with 'completely your call' at line 42 instead of reflecting it.
Participant voiced mental-health motivation; coach replied with generic autonomy statement rather than reflecting or exploring it.

score.summary: Yolanda kept the call structured, with good open questions, a clear goal, a barrier plan, and a summary, but she repeatedly gave the same TV-watching suggestion and often answered change talk with generic autonomy statements. Reflecting Reginald's guilt, mental-health, and grandkids motivations more deeply would have strengthened the partnership.
strengths: Line 5 and line 8 use open questions to check energy and review the last goal.
Line 65 asks an open barrier question ('What might get in the way?') that led to the son-support plan.
Line 67 gives a clear summary that confirms the plan with the participant.
coaching_tips: At line 57, drop the repeated TV suggestion; ask permission or ask what he would find helpful instead.
At line 37, reflect the guilt and desire for energy back to him (e.g., 'Part of you feels bad when you skip, and part of you wants your energy back').
At line 26 and line 41, explore the 'head' and grandkids motivations with an open question such as 'What would it mean to you to keep up with them?'
At line 32, acknowledge his sustain talk before moving on, e.g., 'Food is important to you, and you're not ready to change that.'
